content.thinking:
I need to be careful here since I have very little actual evidence to work with, so I should avoid inventing specific figures and instead use placeholder names in braces when referencing numbers. I'm starting to build the causal chain, beginning with the HighErrorRate alert firing once error rates crossed some threshold, and I need to trace this forward step by step without overstating what's actually known.

Looking at the available evidence, the next step doesn't resolve to a determined root cause — metrics couldn't be read back for the relevant window, and flag history shows no recent changes, with no production changes found either. Since this doesn't converge on a cause, I should mark reaches_a_cause as false and note contributing factors instead, particularly the inability to read metrics, which points to an action item around making metrics retrievable or alerting on telemetry gaps, plus something about an unread paging rule. I'll number these as AI-1 and AI-2, cite the alert for the symptom, use the threshold placeholder where needed, and state plainly that root cause could not be determined given the evidence.

action_items.item: Find out why the per-minute metrics query anchored on the alert time returned no data for io-shop. Fix the metrics collection or the query. Add a check that alerts, or makes the Investigator retry, when the metrics for an alerting service come back empty.

Give the Investigator other evidence sources that do not depend on the metrics store, such as recent deploy or config change history and service logs. Use them when metrics are unavailable. Then re-examine this incident's window by hand to look for the real cause.

causal_chain.step: The HighErrorRate alert fired on io-shop because its error rate was above the threshold for {A1}. The size of the error rate and the number of affected users could not be read.

The cause of the raised error rate was not found. The Investigator asked for per-minute metrics and got back {T5.2} minutes of them, so there was no error or latency data to look at, and it formed no cause that the evidence supports.

Nothing else in the record pointed to a trigger. The flag provider's history showed {T7.2} recent flag changes, so a flag change is ruled out. No production changes or log lines were read, so no code or config change can be named or ruled out. The evidence stops here, and the record does not show why the error rate rose. Argus escalated for insufficient evidence.

contributing_factors.factor: The metrics for the incident window could not be read, so the investigation had no data. The record does not show why the read returned nothing, whether through a gap in collection, a query problem or the anchor time.

No production change history or log lines were read. The only other source Argus used was the flag provider, so it had nothing to work from when metrics failed. The record does not show whether other sources were available.

input.executive_summary: An alert reported that io-shop's error rate was above its threshold. Argus opened an investigation, but it could not read any metrics for the incident window. It also found no recent flag changes, and the record shows no production changes. With nothing to base a cause on, Argus escalated the incident to people. The incident was closed at the same moment it began, so the record gives only a lower bound of {duration} for how long it lasted. The error rate, the number of users affected and the real duration are all unknown. The cause is still undetermined.

went_well: Argus escalated straight away and said plainly that it had insufficient evidence. It did not guess at a cause.
went_wrong: The investigation had no metrics, so it produced no cause and no mitigation.
The error rate, the number of affected users and the real duration could not be established.
How long the paging rule waits before it fires could not be read.

input.root_cause: Not determined. The metrics for the incident window could not be read, and the flag provider showed no recent flag changes, so the record does not show what made io-shop's error rate rise or why.
input.symptom: io-shop requests failed at an elevated rate
